text: Part two, as promised. They bought over five million lottery tickets and won. Did Virginia pay?
Nineteen ninety-two. Twenty-seven million bucks, a state record, won by an Australian fund.
But Virginia investigates. The snag? Tickets had to be bought at a licensed store.
Was this one? Hit like if you'd have double-checked.
About three weeks later: nobody could prove a rule was broken.
So they paid. About one point three million a year, for twenty years.
Send this to the friend who swears the house always wins.
Then Virginia passed emergency rules against bulk buying. Problem— problem solved, right?
Thirty-one years later? Follow, this page finishes the story.
Somebody did it again. Texas, twenty twenty-three, ninety-five million.
It ended with Texas shutting down its lottery commission.
Should a state have to pay? Yes or no.
